runs.name: Eos Energy Enterprises, Inc.
runs.entry: Price **$2.52** (close 2026-10-09, aggregator, flagged) x **364,167,744 shares** (one class, 10-Q cover for 2026-06-30 as of 2026-08-03, 0001628280-26-052906; 340,592,001 on the balance sheet at 2026-06-30, no treasury, the difference the registered direct and rights offerings closed 2026-08-03 and unit releases) = cap **$917.7M**; 218.5M more shares issuable at 2026-02-24 and about 55M added since, not in the count; sovereign **5.60%** (UST 30Y, 2026-10-09). Primary document the FY2025 10-K (0001628280-26-011961), with the 10-Qs to 2026-03-31 and 2026-06-30, the DEF 14A of 2026-04-14 and the 8-Ks of 2026-07-09 to 2026-09-16; cash at 2025-12-31 $567,992 thousand cross-checked to the filed balance sheet. Formerly B. Riley Principal Merger Corp. II (blank-check merger 2020); zinc-based battery energy storage made in the United States, current product the Eos Z3. Lines of evidence derived by the analyst from the 10-K's Items 1, 1A and 7, as the overnight brief directs. **Q1 TOO HARD (NATURE)**: cost of goods above revenue in every filed year (gross margin -911% 2021, -126% 2025 on revenue $114.2M, -74% first half 2026, all after 45X production credits of $21.3M and $22.8M); the filer says it cannot predict customer adoption, that lithium supply exceeds demand and falling lithium prices help Li-ion rivals, and the 45X credits phase down by 2032; two customers 51.5% and 18.8% of 2025 revenue, two 97.7% of Q2 2026; the product changed Gen 2.3 to Z3 Phase 1 to Phase 2 (write-downs) to Indensity. NATURE because the filer has read its own filings and still cannot forecast. The analyst set down the OUT reading ('Start-ups are not our game', Q1's list) and chose TOO HARD on Q1's fixed routing sentence; either closes the file. Q2 to Q12 not reached. Integrity facts recorded, not judged: the 10-K says the January 2025 loan funding meant growth 'without the need to raise additional capital via debt or additional equity offerings' while about $1.5B was raised in 2025; 2025 revenue guidance of $150M-$190M reaffirmed 2025-03-04 against $114.2M reported; $55.0M of Q2 2026 revenue (80%) from an unnamed related party; $112.6M cash plus warrants on 30.0M shares put into Frontier Power USA, controlled by a Cerberus affiliate (lender and preferred holder) and expected to become a customer, with $151.6M of 'Capitalizable joint venture costs' recorded as an asset for the warrants; three people in or acting as CFO since March 2025, the Chief Commercial Officer leaving 2026-10-20; preliminary Q2 results released while the rights offering was open. Beneath the stop, COMPUTATION, NOT A CLEARANCE: owner cash (operating cash plus cash interest, less stock pay, less all capital spending) 2021-2025 -$146.6M, -$225.0M, -$173.3M, -$201.5M, -$282.4M, mean -$205.7M (equity-only -$212.5M); net debt $642.7M on principal after the subsequent events the 10-Q states; range **-$11.85 to -$22.70** a share all-equity (-$10.42 to -$22.27 equity-only), fair -$9.93 all-equity (-$8.58 equity-only); no positive fair price, not armed. Balance sheets 2018-2026-06-30: equity positive only 2020-2021; accumulated deficit $204M (2019) to $2,536M (2025); net income swung by fair-value marks on the company's own warrants and preferred ($233.2M net income on a $163.1M operating loss, first half 2026); cash rises only on financing; borrowings $948.3M principal (carrying $617.1M) plus an $87.0M DOE advance of 2026-09-10, mostly interest paid in kind, secured on substantially all assets, springing maturity 2030, EBITDA and revenue covenants from 2027. Competitors from their own filings (2021-2025 revenue, gross margin): Tesla energy segment $2.8B to $12.8B, -4.6% to 29.8%; Fluence $681M to $2.26B, -10.2% to 13.1%; ESS Tech never above $7.5M, negative throughout; named non-filers flagged (Panasonic, Samsung, LG Chem, BYD, Sungrow, CATL, Enervenue, Ambri, Form Energy). Contamination declared by the analyst: a filename filter over `Test Runs/` for 'eose' or 'eos ' (no match, nothing opened); commit subjects and the memory index in the session context; nothing used. Commits d18afce5 to efd3e3bf. Citations: the analyst's check 29 ids, 19 fragments, 0 problems; the dispatcher's script (`fold_cite_check.py`) 29 ids present, 19 fragments, 0 slips. Position note filled at the fold (not held). check_framework PASS. Analyst's gaps for the operator: (1) the framework does not define a start-up, so Q1's OUT list and its TOO HARD routing can both claim a company with revenue but no gross profit; (2) specific (b) handles a series that changes sign but not one negative at both ends, and the growing-loss bottom of the range is the analyst's reading; the framework could say a range wholly below zero is reported as no positive value and arms no alert; (3) the template asks for the balance sheets in Step 0 when the file closes before Q4 but has no place for them once Step 0 is written. Not read: the S-3ASR of 2026-08-31; the identity of the related-party customer.
runs.narr: Q1 TOO HARD (NATURE): a zinc battery never made at a gross profit (-126% in 2025, -74% in the first half of 2026, after production credits), against a lithium-ion cost curve the filer says is falling and 45X credits that phase down by 2032; the filer says it cannot predict adoption. Integrity facts recorded: a 'no further raises' statement followed by about $1.5B raised in 2025, missed reaffirmed guidance, 80% of a quarter's revenue from a related party, and cash put into a joint venture controlled by its lender. COMPUTATION beneath the stop: owner cash negative every year, fair -$9.93 all-equity against $2.52 (not armed). The analyst asks for a definition of a start-up.
